purpose: Identify the minimum independent verification evidence needed before implementing B03's durable workflow execution, outbox delivery, human waits, and version compatibility. Preserve the complete original B03/AT scope without converting open design choices into assumed behavior.

scope_and_ownership.target: B01 immutable workflow registry plus B02 real PostgreSQL command/outbox persistence, a Temporal execution service, current authorized API projections, and synthetic agent/human adapters. The test environment must distinguish Temporal authority from the Paperclip UI and the G5 filesystem worker.
scope_and_ownership.tc_owner: TC authors independent literal test fixtures/oracles and evidence; code-dev/main owns product implementation and integration; a separate reviewer reviews the plan and evidence. Human submissions in AT-05 must be represented by the authenticated human/task contract once defined, not by agent completion.
scope_and_ownership.scope_limit: Source collection and risk matrix only. No Temporal runtime, external service, tests, or original acceptance case has been executed by this record.
scope_and_ownership.agent_roles: The original agent contract defines code-dev, TC, arch-runner, SQE and report responsibilities. SAM/TEM/static-analysis are worker/validation roles; they are not interchangeable with a human approver or a generic Temporal worker.

test_groups.purpose: Prove accepted durable commands cross the outbox boundary into one pinned workflow execution without confusing HTTP acceptance with execution.
test_groups.target: POST /api/v1/jobs -> command/outbox/workspace-intent transaction -> outbox dispatcher -> Temporal start -> command/job projection and authorized GETs.
test_groups.method: Use real PostgreSQL and the approved Temporal test/runtime environment. Submit an exact valid request with an independent fixed B01 profile/workflow fixture. Inspect the original command receipt, durable outbox record, workflow identity/start input, and database projections at each protocol boundary. Repeat delivery of the same command_id, restart dispatcher, and read job/command through authenticated routes.
test_groups.owner: TC test author; code-dev implements; independent reviewer verifies the fixed oracle.
test_groups.pass_criteria: Exactly one logical workflow start is associated with the original command_id; the command remains accepted until an explicit durable application/rejection under the approved command contract; outbox delivery acknowledgement is recorded separately and cannot itself be treated as application; idempotent replay returns the same receipt/workflow association; no second job or workflow is created. Workspace READY alone never applies a command. Exact projection values and legal transitions must be fixed in the reviewed B03 contract before tests are written.
test_groups.expected_result: The workflow engine is authoritative for process transitions; PostgreSQL retains durable command/outbox and query projection. The job uses B01 workflow identity ifpmic-sw-v1 and a version-pinned execution definition.
test_groups.evidence: Private DB snapshots/transaction identifiers, test-engine history or equivalent deterministic execution trace, command/job GET DTOs, exact command invocations, source hashes, and an evidence ledger mapping every assertion to original contract fields.
test_groups.failure_recovery: Preserve the original DB and Temporal test history privately. Diagnose transaction, dispatch, start, idempotency, or projection boundaries separately. Any semantic change requires a reviewed new candidate and rerun of affected B01/B02 regressions plus B03.
test_groups.unresolved_oracle: The source does not specify outbox claim/lease/ack columns, command applied_revision increment rules, Temporal workflow ID formula, or exact status/error DTO mapping. Do not invent those expected values before the B03 implementation contract is approved.

test_groups.purpose: Demonstrate no command loss or duplicate execution when the API or dispatcher fails at either side of the external workflow-start acknowledgement.
test_groups.target: Crash points after API transaction commit/before outbox delivery; after dispatcher claim/before Temporal start; after Temporal accepts start/before local acknowledgement; after acknowledgement/before projection response; restart and same-command redelivery.
test_groups.method: Inject deterministic process termination/faults at each separately named durable boundary. Restart only the owned test API/dispatcher/Temporal processes. Reconcile by the exact immutable command_id and query workflow history before retrying uncertain starts. Use independent process IDs and durable history; do not infer that a timeout means start failed.
test_groups.owner: TC authors failure harness; code-dev owns dispatcher/engine integration; independent reviewer audits process ownership and replay oracle.
test_groups.pass_criteria: After every restart, the command is recoverable by command_id, no accepted command disappears, at most one effective workflow exists, and an unknown start outcome is reconciled before another start. The same start input/version remains pinned. A retry does not create a second semantic command or change the original accepted receipt.
test_groups.expected_result: AT-16's literal requirement is durable redelivery and duplicate elimination by command_id; it does not specify internal retry timings or claim-state names.
test_groups.evidence: Per-crash-point before/after DB rows, dispatcher process lifecycle, Temporal history and workflow IDs, unique command/workflow counts, retry/reconciliation decisions, and retained private logs with canary scan.
test_groups.failure_recovery: Keep the exact fault point and process evidence. Do not blindly retry an uncertain remote start. Repair reconciliation/idempotency, then rerun the crash point and all normal-start/atomicity cases.
test_groups.unresolved_oracle: The design does not define leases, backoff, poison-message behavior, claim fencing, or how to query a start accepted remotely but not locally acknowledged. These require reviewed protocol decisions.

test_groups.purpose: Prove an agent's completed execution is not enough to pass a human-owned step and that a persistent assigned human task is created and resumed correctly.
test_groups.target: P07 (human-owned, successful path P08) and P21 (human-owned, success P22, business failure P11, design_change_needed P07); workflow states WAITING_HUMAN/READY/SUCCEEDED and human-task persistence/API boundary. Original OpenAPI defines POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/human-submissions (HumanSubmission).
test_groups.method: Drive an agent result with status completed at P07/P21. Verify the workflow blocks in human wait and a durable task appears in the authenticated assignee's worklist. Probe missing, wrong actor, wrong task, duplicate, stale cycle/attempt/version, and conflicting human decisions only after the precise task/submission schema is reviewed. Restart engine/service while waiting, then submit a valid HumanSubmission body (`expected_revision`, `task_id`, `outcome`, `artifact_ids`, `comment`) and verify only the contract-defined next step.
test_groups.owner: TC authors API/engine harness; code-dev integrates; actual human approval is represented only by a synthetic authenticated test actor and is not delegated to agent roles.
test_groups.pass_criteria: No agent completion advances P07/P21 without matching human evidence. The pending task survives restart and is visible only to its authorized actor. A valid submission consumes one task/version once and follows the fixed route; stale or duplicate proof cannot advance the current workflow.
test_groups.expected_result: AT-05 requires a human task and prevents agent-only completion. P07 and P21 have distinct routes and evidence; P21 permits a fixed business failure route to P11 and design_change_needed to P07.
test_groups.evidence: Temporal wait history, task database row and authorized/forbidden API DTOs, exact human submission identity/evidence references, before/after step projection, and restart trace.
test_groups.failure_recovery: Preserve wait/task snapshots. Correct assignment, persistence, authorization, duplicate-submit, or route behavior without synthesizing a human response. Rerun both P07 and P21 plus the AT-05 negative path.
test_groups.unresolved_oracle: The original OpenAPI does define POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/human-submissions and a HumanSubmission schema with required expected_revision, task_id, outcome, artifact_ids and comment. The current FastAPI app has no handler. The data model also names human_tasks and notifications, but does not specify the task-row/assignee resolution, assignment authorization rules, exact outcome-to-P07/P21 transition mapping, or notification event/delivery semantics. B04 owns web/SSE/notification work; the B03/B04 plan must define the boundary without inventing schema fields.

test_groups.purpose: Prove an in-flight v1 workflow waiting for a human resumes with v1 semantics after a v2 definition is deployed, or follows an explicitly approved migration.
test_groups.target: B01 immutable registry (`workflow_id=ifpmic-sw-v1`, `schema_version=1.0.0`), Temporal history/versioning API and worker deployment behavior for an existing P07/P21 human wait.
test_groups.method: Start a workflow under a fixed v1 registry/source fingerprint, drive it to durable WAITING_HUMAN, then introduce a distinct v2 definition/worker build in the controlled test environment. Restart/replay the original history and submit its matching human task. Assert execution either remains on v1-compatible code or uses a specifically reviewed migration record; compare the next transition with the v1 literal workflow fixture.
test_groups.owner: TC authors independent v1/v2 fixtures; code-dev implements version strategy; independent reviewer verifies history and code identity.
test_groups.pass_criteria: The old execution never silently adopts changed v2 transitions or task evidence. It resumes on the pinned v1 behavior, or an explicit migration is durable, versioned, auditable and conforms to a separately approved migration oracle. New jobs may use v2 only under the reviewed activation policy.
test_groups.expected_result: AT-29 explicitly requires v1 semantics on resume, compatible worker retention, or an explicit migration. B01 separates immutable workflow_id from the schema/document format version.
test_groups.evidence: V1/v2 content hashes, Temporal workflow history/replay result, worker build/version identities, persisted task and workflow pin, and before/after projection.
test_groups.failure_recovery: Retain old worker and execution history; do not rewrite or rebase the existing workflow to the new definition. Resolve compatibility policy and rerun old-history replay and new-job selection.
test_groups.unresolved_oracle: No Temporal Worker Versioning/Build ID policy, workflow type-to-workflow_id map, compatibility retention duration, migration record schema, or old-worker retirement rule is specified.

test_groups.purpose: Ensure a new execution authority does not weaken existing auth, idempotency, immutable command, workflow pin, workspace, or safe projection properties.
test_groups.target: G4 `JobService.create/replay/command`, G5 `WorkspaceService` and authenticated job/command endpoints; new worker/dispatcher DB role, events/projection changes and workflow start inputs.
test_groups.method: Re-run accepted G4/G5 regressions against the B03 candidate. Assert API-owned command inputs remain immutable; worker identity is scoped; direct SQL/API callers cannot forge applied status or workflow transitions; unauthorized users cannot read another job/task; raw prompt/tool/provider secrets are not projected; workspace READY remains distinct from workflow execution. Verify GET command changes only after a durable defined engine outcome.
test_groups.owner: TC authors regression and role tests; code-dev owns migrations/service; independent reviewer audits no-authority leakage.
test_groups.pass_criteria: The original accepted receipt remains traceable; owner/project/session and scoped worker authorization remain enforced; no API 202 or workspace READY is treated as applied/executed; projections are derived from authoritative persisted/Temporal state and do not expose hidden reasoning, raw commands, credentials, or unredacted tool I/O.
test_groups.expected_result: B03 adds an execution layer while preserving B01/B02 boundaries and the original OpenAPI semantics.
test_groups.evidence: Fresh G4/G5 test IDs and fingerprints, DB grants, authorized/unauthorized DTO comparisons, source/payload redaction checks, job-command-workspace relationship counts.
test_groups.failure_recovery: Do not accept B03 with a G4/G5 regression. Restore safe projections/role boundaries, run affected suites, then repeat B03 crash/human/version tests.
test_groups.unresolved_oracle: The current schema intentionally denies runtime updates to jobs, commands and outbox. B03 needs a reviewed least-privilege worker/Temporal projection migration; exact actor/worker credential and event projection fields are not yet defined.

cross_cutting_normal_exception_boundary_.normal: One accepted command starts once, uses the immutable workflow pin, exposes a durable authorized projection, and pauses at human-owned nodes until valid human evidence is submitted.
cross_cutting_normal_exception_boundary_.exception: API/dispatcher/Temporal process crash, timeout, duplicate delivery/start, DB rollback, remote-accepted/local-unknown start, worker restart, duplicate human submission, and version deployment while waiting.
cross_cutting_normal_exception_boundary_.boundary: Commit versus dispatch/start/ack/projection cut points; exact authorized actor/task and cycle/attempt/version; P07/P21 state routes; v1 history replay when v2 code is present; command receipt remains accepted until an explicit durable result.
cross_cutting_normal_exception_boundary_.regression: B01 source/workflow content hashes, G4 transactional four-row command group and permissions, G5 workspace preparation/lease/recovery, API owner/session scope, and prohibition on reading hidden execution data.

open_questions_for_approved_b03_plan: Define which persistent store owns Temporal event history versus IFPMIC business projections, and how Temporal IDs bind to command_id, job_id, project_id and workflow_id.
Specify outbox state/claim/lease/fencing/ack fields, dispatch transaction boundaries, backoff, visibility timeout, poison-command handling and at-most-one effective Temporal start reconciliation.
Specify the least-privilege Temporal/worker database role and idempotent projection activities; current runtime grants explicitly cannot apply commands/outbox or change job status.
Define exact command application/rejection state transitions, expected_revision behavior and `applied_revision` increments without changing POST 202 acceptance semantics.
Define human task storage, assignment, authentication/authorization, submission endpoint, one-effective-completion rule and interaction with B04 notifications/events.
Define version pin mapping from B01 `workflow_id` to Temporal workflow type/version/build; specify v1 worker compatibility and explicit migration semantics before testing AT-29.
Choose deterministic test support for external start accepted before acknowledgement is lost; a local fake that does not model durable Temporal history cannot alone prove AT-16.

acceptance_status.AT-05: not_executed; current G4/G5 evidence does not create operational human work items
acceptance_status.AT-16: not_executed; current outbox remains pending and no dispatcher exists
acceptance_status.AT-29: not_executed; B01 pins static registry content but no Temporal running history/version compatibility exists
acceptance_status.B04_and_later: separate backlog scope; event/SSE and notification delivery must not be claimed through this matrix
acceptance_status.original_AT_01_to_AT_32: remain not_executed until individually run against their approved acceptance contracts

evidence_and_recovery_policy.evidence_path: Future reviewed B03 test ledger and private per-attempt database/Temporal/process records; do not place raw credentials, prompts, tool input/output or unrestricted service logs in public evidence.
evidence_and_recovery_policy.failure_handling: Preserve failing source bytes, DB lifecycle, workflow history and exact crash point. A failed or timed-out remote start is an unknown outcome to reconcile, never an automatic blind retry.
evidence_and_recovery_policy.scope_change: Any change to workflow version semantics, human submission contract, outbox acknowledgment policy or command status projection requires a new reviewed contract and affected G4/G5 regression reruns.

human_submission.response: 202 CommandReceipt; acceptance remains distinct from completed work
human_submission.implementation_status: Defined in original OpenAPI, but no handler is present in current services/ifpmic_api/app.py
